chapter_theme: A song at Poomparai (பூம்பறை): the poet asks whether a relationship with price-women who speak of kinship and seek out rich houses can be right; the praise names Krishna dancing on the serpent.

620.reading: The poet describes women with bodies soft as mango shoots who talk of kinship, look for houses where men live well, make friends, smear sandal on their breasts and play until their waists ache, and asks whether a shameless relationship with such price-women can be right. The praise names Krishna who danced to rhythm on the serpent's heads and helped the Pandavas, Murugan his nephew, and the groves of vengai, palasa and plantain and the flowering tanks of Poomparai.
620.nuance: விலைமாதர், price-women, is the plainest name; முறை பேசி, talking of kinship, is their false familiarity, and வாழ்ந்த மனை தேடி, seeking out prosperous houses, their motive. பாந்தள் முடிமீது ... நடமாடு is Krishna's dance on Kaliya.

links.note: 620 describes price-women (விலைமாதர்) who talk of kinship (முறை பேசி) while looking for prosperous houses (வாழ்ந்த மனை தேடி). Kural 912 names the same move: women who weigh the gain and then speak of their virtue (பயன்தூக்கிப் பண்புரைக்கும்), and tells the man to weigh them in return. The song's scene is the couplet's charge acted out.
